A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMPspec research by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation results, causal Bayesian optimization experiments including a healthcare simulator, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds robustness and sensitivity results, plus a 401(k) data analysis with runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects the coverage check from each bootstrap posterior mean falling inside its own interval to a fixed plug-in estimate falling inside bootstrap intervals. This aligns the pseudocode with the separate plug-in estimator already described in v2's appendices. The GP priors, posterior formulas, training objectives, and principal inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds the 9,915-observation 401(k) dataset, evaluating income-dependent effects of binary pension-plan eligibility on financial assets. It also adds toy scenarios with Student-t outcome noise and skewed Beta treatment sampling. The original toy, synthetic causal graph, and healthcare-simulator coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds orthogonal random forests, implemented with DMLOrthoForest, to the synthetic benchmark comparison in Table 2 and Figure 4. Continuous DR, Sampling GP, and BayesIMP remain; the original toy and CBO comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds interval-score evaluation, including IS95 in Tables 1–2 and IS90/IS95 in robustness tests. New protocols include ORF response-curve reconstruction with an oracle intercept and the 401(k) experiment's standardization, minibatch training, and income-quantile evaluation grid. These additions do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained calibration, sample-splitting, and BayesIMP ablations, v3 adds sensitivity to bootstrap replication counts and kernel choice, plus heavy-tailed-noise and limited-support robustness tests (Tables 6–8). These examine additional questions about calibration stability and model misspecification.

E5.justification: v3 adds explicit seed-zero disclosure for the 401(k) experiment and examines calibration bootstrap counts of 10, 20, 50, and 100. The existing 50-trial experiments and 100 bootstrap replications for calibration-summary uncertainty remain; no increase in repetitions for the original results is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds ORF scores, interval scores, sensitivity and robustness results, and 401(k) effect and computational findings. For example, Table 2 reports IS95 of 2.27 for IMPspec and 2.99 for BayesIMP. Existing main-table RMSE/calibration values are largely retained with rounding. Table 2 drops explicit out-of-support calibration averages, although Figure 4 retains the corresponding curves.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 derives posterior chi-squared, total-variation, and moment-error bounds under likelihood-ratio moment control, separating surrogate-likelihood error from Gaussian approximation error. Appendix C.2.5 also adds an argmin-consistency argument for calibration grid search. The original posterior-moment and calibration-estimator proofs are largely retained after relocation.

C1.justification: The central spectral GP/RKHS and calibration contributions remain. v3 frames the empirical contribution as improved uncertainty quantification with competitive effect estimation and explicitly extends its practical claims to a large real dataset; v2 emphasizes state-of-the-art uncertainty quantification and CBO performance on simulations and the healthcare example.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands discussion of surrogate-likelihood validity, Gaussian approximation limitations, and the restrictions of calibration within a chosen spectral family. It explains ORF's limitations through its linear treatment-response model and explicitly treats 401(k) as a plausibility and feasibility study without ground-truth causal effects. These qualifications go beyond v2's brief surrogate-model explanation.

D1.justification: v3 supplies extensive 401(k) loading, preprocessing, training, calibration, covariance-computation, and resource-measurement details. It adds ORF configuration and documents the already evaluated Continuous DR baseline's fixed-B=0 adaptation and nuisance-estimation procedures. The latter is newly disclosed information, not evidence of changed implementation. The code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 broadens Bayesian causal-inference context with Alaa and Van Der Schaar, Hahn et al., and Oganisian and Roy, and adds ORF-related positioning. It removes the previous GP predictive-calibration discussion and associated citations. The central relationship to Singh et al. and BayesIMP remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, related work, and experimental narrative. It adds a Discussion section, consolidates evaluation-metric explanations, and moves experimental appendices ahead of the mathematical proofs. This is substantial restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 changes document and plot typography, reformats algorithms, restructures Tables 1–2, and adds the 401(k) figure and several tables. Figure 4 gains ORF curves. The existing CBO convergence plot moves from v2's appendix Figure 7 to main-text Figure 5; it is not a new experiment.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evaluation of its central uncertainty claims through interval scores, misspecification and support tests, and documented real-data feasibility. Appendix A.4 and the Discussion also make approximation limits more explicit. Some qualifications remain: 401(k) cannot validate causal coverage, and Table 8's claim of best interval scores overlooks Sampling GP's slightly better limited-support IS90. These issues do not outweigh the broader gains in validation and transparency.
